source_snapshot.procedure: Launch KVM, GET Redfish sessions, close KVM, wait five minutes and GET sessions again.
source_snapshot.criteria: Session information is visible and the KVM session closes within five minutes after KVM close.
source_snapshot.script: No Master command; 10 attended/10 machine minutes; unique row/code/variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; preserves open/close/poll timing but does not prove which session entry belongs to KVM and exposes hardcoded credentials.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/MEDIUM; requires exact KVM-to-session mapping, configured timeout/grace, protected polling and unrelated-session invariants.

old_problem: BMC Web, KVM websocket and Redfish SessionService may represent different lifecycles. Anonymous before/after lists could mistake another user's session closure for success, and the five-minute boundary/mapped terminal representation were unspecified.
disposition_reason: The launch/close/timing objective is clear. ED-06/15/20 allow the firmware-specific KVM session resource/correlation fields, configured timeout and grace as project configuration. A dedicated account, differential inventory and bounded read-only polling uniquely track the test session without closing unrelated sessions or exposing secrets.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2242, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2243 / Wistron-BMC Sanity-00025-V001 / 252628d2ae3a62d9 was directly read from XLSX and its historical record.
Bind BMC/SUT/WebUI/KVM versions and prove whether standard SessionService or a documented vendor resource represents KVM connections.
Use a dedicated account and redacted baseline session inventory; launch one KVM and verify fresh correct-target connection/video without keyboard, mouse, media or power input.
Map the added session by approved non-secret account/client/origin/creation-time/vendor metadata and record its URI or salted ID hash.
Close KVM normally, timestamp it, and poll read-only at bounded intervals through five minutes plus approved grace; do not terminate sessions via API.
Require only the mapped record to become absent/deleted/terminal as specified and prove all unrelated session identifiers remain stable.
Protect credentials/tokens/Authorization headers and stop on wrong target, ambiguous mapping, API error, token leak or unrelated-session change; no blind retry.
No login, KVM launch/close, Redfish poll, session termination, retry or DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: Mapped KVM session lifecycle and five-minute close timeout
test_case.purpose: Verify that one authorized KVM connection maps to the expected session record and that normal KVM close transitions that exact record to the documented closed/expired state within five minutes without affecting other sessions.
required_package: BMC/SUT/WebUI/KVM versions and supported KVM session resource/schema
Dedicated account and approved non-secret session-correlation fields
Configured timeout, five-minute boundary, polling interval/grace and terminal representation
Trusted TLS/secret/session-redaction, concurrent-session baseline and cleanup/recovery
test_case.test_command: Capture a redacted baseline session inventory, launch one dedicated correctly mapped KVM, identify the added record by approved correlation fields, close KVM normally, timestamp close, and poll the mapped read-only session resource at bounded intervals through five minutes plus approved grace while proving unrelated session IDs remain unchanged.
test_case.expected_result: The correct KVM session is uniquely identified while open and becomes absent/deleted or terminal exactly as documented within the five-minute/grace boundary after normal close; all unrelated sessions remain stable and no sensitive token/input is exposed.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires unique KVM-to-session correlation, complete open/close/poll timeline and mapped terminal/absence within threshold with unrelated sessions unchanged. Anonymous list differences, another session ending, unsupported collection, ambiguous mapping or timeout exceedance is not PASS. Missing mapping/policy blocks execution, not review.
safety_gate: Verify correct KVM target, dedicated account and session mapping before timing.
No keyboard/mouse/power/virtual-media action, API termination or unrelated-session close.
Redact credentials, tokens and sensitive payloads; use TLS-validated access.
Stop on wrong target, ambiguous mapping, token leak, API error or unrelated-session change.
expected_evidence: Dedicated account approval and redacted baseline session inventory
Fresh correct-target KVM visual/connection evidence plus mapped session URI/salted ID and fields
Close timestamp and bounded poll timeline through five minutes/grace
Mapped terminal/absence result, unrelated-session invariants and cleanup/no-secret audit
test_case.recovery: On mapping or access anomaly, do not close API resources or retry login blindly. Preserve redacted evidence, close only the known test KVM under the signed plan, and use the recovery account to verify unrelated sessions/access.

source_conflict.reason: The source consistently uses session data to observe KVM open/close and five-minute cleanup; mapping is a vendor prerequisite.

blocked.reason: The lifecycle method is clear; resource mapping, timeout and terminal semantics are parameterizable.
